meta.instrument: SEBI (Depositories and Participants) Regulations, 2018 - No. SEBI/LAD-NRO/GN/2018/40, Gazette of India Extraordinary Part III Section 4, 3 October 2018
meta.authored: Read from the held text, provision by provision. NOT generated from master sheet.xlsx - unlike ca_master.json, lodr_*.json and pit_master.json, which build_master.py and build_lodr.py generate from the owner's spreadsheet and which must not be hand-edited. This file is hand-authored against reference/ and every rule carries the words it came from in `quote`.
meta.scope: ONLY the obligations this regulation places on the ISSUER. The regulation also binds depositories (Reg 41-57, 73, 82), participants (Reg 58-69, 81) and beneficial owners (Reg 74(1), 79(1)). Those are separate regulated entities and giving a listed company NSDL's obligations would be the SS2z defect - wrong law against the wrong entity class. Checked one by one: Reg 81 binds 'a depository and a participant', Reg 82 'a depository', Reg 65 'every participant'. All excluded.
meta.applicability: Marked listed-only. Reg 76 requires submission 'to the concerned stock exchanges', which only a listed issuer has. The other obligations bind any issuer whose securities are eligible for dematerialisation - which for unlisted public and private companies is triggered by Rule 9A / 9B of the Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules 2014, and those Rules are NOT in reference/. Asserting them would be guessing at law this project does not hold (same treatment as PAS-3 under Rule 12, SS2n, and BEN-2 under the SBO Rules, SS2o). Each rule says so in `notes`.

rules.title: Agreement with the depository
rules.detail: Enter into an agreement with the depository, in accordance with Reg 43, once the securities are declared eligible to be held in dematerialised form.
rules.quote: Every issuer whose securities have been declared as eligible to be held in dematerialised form in a depository shall enter into an agreement with the depository in accordance with the provisions of regulation 43
rules.frequency: On eligibility; on adding a depository
rules.appliesToText: Issuer whose securities are eligible for dematerialisation
rules.notes: The proviso excludes the case where the depository is itself the issuer, and Government securities issued by the State or the Central Government. For an UNLISTED issuer the demat trigger comes from Rule 9A/9B of the PAS Rules 2014, which is not in reference/.

rules.title: Share registry work handled at a single point
rules.detail: Transfer of securities, records of holders, handling of physical securities and depository connectivity must all sit at ONE point - either in-house or with a SEBI-registered Share Transfer Agent. Splitting them between the two is the breach.
rules.quote: All matters relating to transfer of securities, maintenance of records of holders of securities, handling of physical securities and establishing connectivity with the depositories shall be handled and maintained at a single point i.e. either in-house by the issuer or by a Share Transfer Agent registered with the Board
rules.appliesToText: Issuer whose securities are eligible for dematerialisation
rules.evidence: RTA agreement and SEBI registration, or the in-house arrangement and board record
rules.notes: The test is single-point, not competence: work divided between an in-house team and an RTA breaches this even if both do it well.

rules.title: Redress beneficial owners' grievances within thirty days
rules.detail: Redress a beneficial owner's grievance within thirty days of receiving the complaint, and keep the depository informed of the number and nature redressed and the number pending.
rules.quote: Every issuer or its agent or any person who is registered as an intermediary under this regulation, shall redress the grievances of beneficial owners within thirty days of the date of receipt of the complaint and keep the depository informed about the number and nature of grievances redressed by it and the number of grievances pending before it
rules.timelineText: Within thirty days of the date of receipt of the complaint

due.when: Within thirty days of receipt of the complaint

rules.evidence: Grievance register with receipt and redressal dates; intimation to the depository
rules.notes: The clock runs from RECEIPT of the complaint, not from any later triage. There is a second, separate duty in the same regulation - telling the depository the counts - which is easy to miss because the thirty days draws the eye. This register does not hold investor complaints, so no date is computed; record it against the complaint.

rules.title: Confirm dematerialisation to the depository within fifteen days
rules.detail: Within fifteen days of receiving the certificate from the participant: confirm to the depository that the securities are listed, mutilate and cancel the certificate, substitute the depository as registered owner in the records, and send a certificate to the depository and to every exchange where the security is listed.
rules.quote: Within fifteen days of receipt of the certificate of security from the participant the issuer shall confirm to the depository that securities comprised in the said certificate have been listed on the stock exchange or exchanges where the earlier issued securities are listed and shall also after due verification immediately mutilate and cancel the certificate of security and substitute in its record the name of the depository as the registered owner and shall send a certificate to this effect to the depository and to every stock exchange where the security is listed
rules.timelineText: Within fifteen days of receipt of the certificate from the participant

due.when: Within fifteen days of receipt from the participant

rules.evidence: Demat request register; confirmation to depository; cancelled certificates; exchange intimation
rules.notes: Four separate acts inside one fifteen-day period, and the cancellation of the certificate is the one most often left undone. The proviso removes only the LISTING condition for unlisted companies - the rest of the sub-regulation still applies to them.

rules.title: Maintain a record of dematerialised certificates
rules.detail: Keep a record of the certificates of securities that have been dematerialised.
rules.quote: The issuer shall maintain a record of certificates of securities which have been dematerialised
rules.notes: Distinct from the register of members. This is the record of what was surrendered and cancelled.

rules.title: Reconcile dematerialised securities daily
rules.detail: Reconcile the records of dematerialised securities against all securities issued, every day.
rules.quote: The issuer or its agent shall reconcile the records of dematerialised securities with all the securities issued by the issuer, on a daily basis
rules.evidence: Daily reconciliation output retained by the issuer or the RTA
rules.notes: DAILY, not quarterly - the quarterly item is the Reg 76 audit report, which reports on this reconciliation. They are two different duties and the daily one is the one usually delegated to the RTA and never evidenced by the issuer. The proviso moves the duty to the depository only for Government securities.

rules.title: Quarterly Reconciliation of Share Capital Audit report to the stock exchanges
rules.detail: Submit a quarterly audit report to the stock exchanges, audited by a qualified Chartered Accountant, a practising Company Secretary or a practising Cost Accountant, reconciling total issued capital, listed capital and capital held in dematerialised form, with the changes in share capital during the quarter and the in-principle approvals obtained for further issued capital.
rules.quote: Every issuer shall submit audit report on a quarterly basis, starting from September 30, 2003, to the concerned stock exchanges audited by a qualified Chartered Accountant or a practicing Company Secretary or a practicing Cost Accountant, for the purposes of reconciliation of the total issued capital, listed capital and capital held by depositories in dematerialized form, the details of changes in share capital during the quarter and the in-principle approval obtained by the issuer from all the stock exchanges where it is listed in respect of such further issued capital
rules.appliesToText: Listed issuer - the report goes to the stock exchanges
rules.evidence: Signed audit report; exchange filing acknowledgement
rules.signedBy: Practising Company Secretary / Chartered Accountant / Cost Accountant
rules.notes: NO DEADLINE IS STATED. Reg 76(1) fixes the cadence - quarterly - and says nothing about when in the quarter it is due. The period comes from SEBI circulars and exchange requirements that are NOT in reference/, so no date is computed here (SS2k: a rule with no offset must not carry a date). The SEBI LODR Master Circular of 30 January 2026 confirms this report is within the single filing system alongside Reg 13(3), Reg 27(2) and Reg 44(3), but states no period for it either. This is the engagement a practising CS is most often appointed for under this regulation.

rules.title: Demat requests within twenty-one days, and delays explained in the report
rules.detail: The quarterly report must also give the updated status of the register of members and confirm that securities were dematerialised within twenty-one days of the issuer receiving the request - and where they were not, disclose the reasons for the delay.
rules.quote: The audit report under sub-regulation (1) shall also give the updated status of the register of members of the issuer and confirm that securities have been dematerialized as per requests within twenty one days from the date of receipt of requests by the issuer and where the dematerialization has not been effected within the said stipulated period, the report shall disclose the reasons for such delay
rules.timelineText: Within twenty one days from the date of receipt of the request

due.when: Within twenty one days of receipt of the demat request

rules.evidence: Demat request register with receipt and completion dates; delay reasons where applicable
rules.notes: A service standard the auditor must report against, so a delay is not merely operational - it is disclosed to the exchanges every quarter. Note this twenty-one days runs from the ISSUER's receipt of the request, while the fifteen days in Reg 74(5) runs from receipt of the CERTIFICATE from the participant. Two clocks, two anchors, same transaction.

rules.title: Report any capital difference immediately
rules.detail: Immediately bring to the notice of the depositories and the stock exchanges any difference observed between issued capital, listed capital and capital held in dematerialised form.
rules.quote: The issuer shall immediately bring to the notice of the depositories and the stock exchanges, any difference observed in its issued, listed, and the capital held by depositories in dematerialised form
rules.evidence: Intimation to depositories and exchanges with the date observed
rules.notes: Immediate, and NOT deferred to the next quarterly report. Waiting for the Reg 76(1) audit to surface a difference the issuer had already observed is itself the breach.

rules.title: Maintain continuous electronic connectivity with the depository
rules.detail: Establish continuous electronic means of communication with every depository with which an agreement has been entered into.
rules.quote: Every issuer or its agent shall establish continuous electronic means of communication with the depository with which it has entered into an agreement
rules.evidence: Connectivity arrangement with the RTA or depository; downtime log
rules.notes: In practice discharged through the RTA, which does not move the duty off the issuer.

rules.title: Inform the depository of book closures, record dates and meeting dates
rules.detail: Give the depository information about book closures, record dates, interest and dividend payment dates, annual general meeting and other meeting dates, debenture redemption and conversion dates, call money dates and other such information, at the time and in the manner the depository's bye-laws or the agreement specify.
rules.quote: Every issuer whose securities have been declared as eligible for dematerialisation in a depository shall give information to the depository about book closures, record dates, dates for the payment of interest or dividend, dates for annual general meetings and other meetings, dates for redemption of debentures, dates for conversion of debentures and warrants, call money dates and such other information at the time and in the manner as may be specified by the depository in its bye-laws or agreement
rules.timelineText: As specified by the depository's bye-laws or the agreement
rules.appliesToText: Issuer whose securities are eligible for dematerialisation
rules.evidence: Intimation to the depository per corporate action, with dates
rules.notes: The regulation DELEGATES the timing - 'at the time and in the manner as may be specified by the depository in its bye-laws or agreement'. NSDL and CDSL bye-laws are not in reference/, so no period is asserted here. This runs alongside the LODR Reg 42 record-date intimation to the exchanges, which is a separate filing to a separate recipient. The proviso excludes Government securities.
